# How to read this report

Everything below is read from files written by `00`-`04`; nothing is typed in. It is a
**simulation**: genetic parameters come from the literature (file 00), but the population,
its genomes and its phenotypes are simulated, so results show what the *design* implies,
not what real Nordic data would show. Units are **genetic standard deviations of the founder
population** unless stated. GS_NTM, GS_NTM_NUE35, GS_NTM_NUE75, GS_NTM_NUE35_MUN, the methane scenario (`r ch4_sc`) and
GS_NTM_NUE35_OCS_dF1 were run with up to **`r params$n_rep` replicates, each from its own independent
coalescent founder population and burn-in** (7 Nov 2026, my choice); PHENO and GS_NTM_NUE35_MATE
once (replicate 0). Within a replicate all scenarios share the founders, burn-in and random-number
stream, so scenario differences are paired. Only the replicate section tests whether a difference
between programmes is consistent; single-run differences in the earlier tables are indicative only.
Genomic EBVs in file 04 came from **`r eval_model`**, the winner of the head-to-head test in `04b`. Genomic-prediction accuracies come from one cross-validation run
per dataset (3 folds + forward), so differences below about 0.05 are within fold-to-fold noise.

# Genetic parameters used (file 00)

```{r params}
h2 <- fread("params/h2.csv")
kable(h2[, .(trait, code, HOL, RDC, JER, status, source)], caption = "Heritabilities and their sources")
```

# Breeding goal: NTM weights and the expected price of NUE (file 00)

The indices use the official **NTM sub-index weights (May 2026)** for the five sub-indices that
have a simulated counterpart (Yield = milk + protein yield with Kargo et al. 2014 economic values,
Fertility = ICF, Udder health = SCS, Longevity, Saved Feed = SF, the NAV Saved Feed trait since
7 Nov 2026). NTM has no weight for NUE, MUN or CH4; NUE is added at 0.35 (the Saved Feed weight) or
0.75, MUN at -0.35 on top of NUE 0.35, and CH4 on top of one NUE weight at the knee of the CH4
weight sweep (file 00; chosen: `r ch4_sc`, CH4 weight `r idx_def[index == ch4_sc, ch4]`). Mapping and assumptions: file 00.

```{r goal}
kable(dcast(iw[weight != 0 | trait %in% c("NUE", "MUN", "CH4")], trait ~ index + breed, value.var = "weight"), digits = 3,
      caption = "Index weights per genetic SD (other traits 0)")
sw <- if (file.exists("params/ch4_weight_sweep.csv")) fread("params/ch4_weight_sweep.csv") else NULL
if (!is.null(sw)) print(ggplot(melt(sw, id.vars = c("nue", "ch4_weight"), measure.vars = c("CH4", "NUE", "ntm_lost_pct")),
         aes(-ch4_weight, value)) + geom_line() + facet_grid(variable ~ nue, scales = "free_y", labeller = label_both) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, lty = 3) + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "negative CH4 weight (dotted = chosen knee, 0.50)", y = NULL,
       title = "CH4 weight sweep (file 00, selection-index theory, cow-weighted)"))
fr <- fread("params/ntm_nue_frontier.csv")
kable(fr[nue_weight %in% c(0, 0.35, 0.75), .(breed, nue_weight, NUE, MUN, CH4, MY, PY, NTM_pct_of_max, EUR_loss_per_cow_yr)],
      digits = 3, caption = "Selection-index theory (true breeding values, per unit selection intensity): responses in genetic SD, NTM value kept, EUR per cow-year lost")
```

# Heritability recovered from the simulated data (file 02)

```{r vc}
vc <- rd("vc_gblup.csv")
if (!is.null(vc)) kable(vc, digits = 3,
  caption = "GBLUP- and ABLUP-REML h2 vs the true h2 within breed x generation (FULL data, 1,500 genotyped / 3,000 phenotyped cows)")
```

`r if (!is.null(vc)) { vc[, rG := h2_GBLUP_REML / h2_true_genotyped]; vc[, rA := h2_ABLUP_REML / h2_true_genotyped] }; ""`
Genomic REML relative to the true within-breed h^2^ (ratio): `r if (!is.null(vc)) paste(vc[order(rG), sprintf("%s %.2f", trait, rG)], collapse = ", ") else "n/a"`.
A ratio below 1 is genetic variance the SNP panel (about 10k) does not capture (de los Campos et al. 2015).
Pedigree REML was within 20% of the true value for `r if (!is.null(vc)) paste(vc[abs(rA - 1) <= 0.2, trait], collapse = ", ") else "n/a"`
and further off for `r if (!is.null(vc)) paste(vc[abs(rA - 1) > 0.2, sprintf("%s (%.2f)", trait, rA)], collapse = ", ") else "n/a"`;
with 3,000 records, low-h^2^ traits carry little information.

# Genomic prediction: cross-validated accuracy (file 02)

Every model fits **breed** and herd x generation as fixed effects (file 02), so no model
estimates the genetic differences *between* breeds, and file 04 selects *within* breed. The
accuracy that matters is therefore the **within-breed** correlation between EBV and true
breeding value (averaged over breeds, weighted by cows). The pooled correlation over all three
breeds is shown second, because it also rewards or penalises arbitrary breed-level offsets in
the EBVs.

```{r cv}
traits_cv <- c("NUE", "MUN", "SF", "CH4")
cv <- rbindlist(lapply(traits_cv, function(t) rd(sprintf("cv_results_%s.csv", t))), fill = TRUE)
cv9 <- rd("cv_results_NUE.csv", params$gxe_dir)
if (!is.null(cv9)) cv <- rbind(cv, cv9[, trait := "NUE_rg0.9"], fill = TRUE)
cv <- cv[model != "GBLUP_snp"]
cvs <- cv[, .(acc_wb = mean(acc_within_breed), acc = mean(acc_TBV), slope = mean(slope)),
          by = .(trait, model, scheme = ifelse(scheme == "forward", "forward", "k-fold"))]
kable(dcast(cvs, model ~ trait + scheme, value.var = "acc_wb"), digits = 3,
      caption = "Within-breed accuracy = cor(EBV, true BV) within breed, n-weighted mean (the accuracy that matters for selection)")
kable(dcast(cvs, model ~ trait + scheme, value.var = "acc"), digits = 3,
      caption = "Pooled accuracy across the three breeds (sensitive to breed-level EBV offsets; for transparency)")
ggplot(cv[scheme != "forward"], aes(model, acc_within_breed, fill = model)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) + facet_wrap(~trait) + theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) + labs(x = NULL, y = "within-breed accuracy (k-fold)")
best <- cvs[!is.na(acc_wb), .SD[which.max(acc_wb)], by = .(trait, scheme)]
```

```{r cv_dispersion}
# forward validation (youngest, unrecorded generation): EBVs saved by file 02
ef <- rbindlist(lapply(traits_cv, function(t) rd(sprintf("ebv_forward_%s.csv", t))), fill = TRUE)
mods <- intersect(c("ABLUP", "GBLUP", "ssGBLUP", "ssGBLUP_MF", "wssGBLUP", "rrBLUP", "BayesA", "BayesB"), names(ef))
el <- melt(ef, id.vars = c("trait", "id", "breed", "TBV"), measure.vars = mods,
           variable.name = "model", value.name = "EBV")
el[, `:=`(tc = TBV - mean(TBV), ec = EBV - mean(EBV)), by = .(trait, model, breed)]
disp <- el[, .(slope_wb = sum(tc * ec) / sum(ec^2)), by = .(trait, model)]
kable(dcast(disp, model ~ trait, value.var = "slope_wb"), digits = 2,
      caption = "Forward validation, dispersion within breed: regression of true BV on EBV after centring both by breed (1 = unbiased; < 1 = over-dispersed)")
off <- el[trait == "NUE", .(TBV = mean(TBV), EBV = mean(EBV)), by = .(model, breed)]
offw <- dcast(off, model ~ breed, value.var = "EBV")
offw <- rbind(data.table(model = "true BV", t(setNames(off[model == mods[1], TBV], off[model == mods[1], breed]))), offw, fill = TRUE)
kable(offw, digits = 2, caption = "NUE, forward validation: breed means of true BV and of each model's EBV")
s_nue <- cvs[trait == "NUE" & model == "ssGBLUP" & scheme == "forward"]
jer_low <- off[model == "ssGBLUP"][order(EBV)]$breed[1]
f2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
bw <- function(tr, sc) { b <- best[trait == tr & scheme == sc]; sprintf("%s (%.2f)", b$model, b$acc_wb) }
wss_h2 <- range(cv[model == "wssGBLUP", h2_REML_fit], na.rm = TRUE)
```

**Cross-examination of the working assumption that ssGBLUP gives good EBVs.**

`r arc <- "archive_rg9_2026-11-03/sim_FULL_rg1.00/cv_results_NUE.csv"; a_nue <- if (file.exists(arc)) fread(arc)[model == "ssGBLUP" & scheme == "forward"] else NULL; ord_ok <- identical(off[model == "ssGBLUP"][order(-EBV)]$breed, off[model == mods[1]][order(-TBV)]$breed); ""`
* *Breed-level offsets in single-step EBVs.* In this run ssGBLUP's pooled NUE accuracy in the
  youngest generation was `r f2(s_nue$acc)` (slope `r f2(s_nue$slope)`) against a within-breed
  accuracy of `r f2(s_nue$acc_wb)`, and its breed means were
  `r if (ord_ok) "in the same order as the true breed means" else paste0("not in the order of the true breed means (", jer_low, " ranked lowest)")`.
  `r if (!is.null(a_nue)) sprintf("In the archived run with the 9-correlation matrix (1-3 Nov), the same model gave a pooled accuracy of %s against %s within breed, because it ranked the breed with the highest true mean lowest.", f2(mean(a_nue$acc_TBV)), f2(mean(a_nue$acc_within_breed))) else ""`
  So the breed-level part of single-step EBVs is unstable between runs. Because breed is a
  fixed effect, that part carries no information in any model, and it is consistent with the
  known incompatibility between the genomic matrix G and the pedigree matrix A~22~ (different
  bases and genetic means) in single-step evaluation (Vitezica et al. 2011, *Genet Res*
  93:357-366). **Correction (7 Nov 2026):** an earlier version said that no adjustment was tested.
  In fact `ssGBLUP` has always used G rescaled to A~22~ (a + bG, Christensen et al. 2012), pooled over
  the three breeds. Since 7 Nov the breed-metafounder model (`ssGBLUP_MF`; Legarra et al. 2015,
  *Genetics* 200:455-468) is fitted alongside it; the comparison is below.
* *Pooled-adjusted G vs metafounders.* `r ch <- rbindlist(lapply(traits_cv, function(t) rd(sprintf("ssgblup_choice_%s.csv", t))), fill = TRUE); cp <- rd("G_A22_compatibility.csv"); if (nrow(ch)) paste0("Chosen per trait (decision rule of file 02: within-breed accuracy, ties within 1 SE broken by dispersion slope): ", paste(sprintf("%s %s (MF minus pooled %+.3f, SE %.3f)", ch$focus_traits, ch$winner, ch$mean_diff_acc_MF_minus_pooled, ch$se_diff), collapse = "; "), ".") else "Not available."`
  `r if (!is.null(cp)) sprintf("Mean gap between G and A22 relationships across breed blocks: pooled-adjusted %.3f, metafounder %.3f (absolute mean over blocks; file 02). ", mean(abs(cp$gap_pooled)), mean(abs(cp$gap_MF))) else ""`Why this matters: with pooled rescaling the between-breed blocks of G and A~22~ cannot all match at
  once, so EBVs carry an arbitrary breed offset; metafounders give each breed its own base, so G~05~
  and A^Γ^~22~ agree by construction. Within-breed ranking, which is what file 04 uses, is affected
  only through the within-breed blocks.
* *Within breed, the best model was:* NUE `r bw("NUE", "k-fold")` k-fold and
  `r bw("NUE", "forward")` forward; MUN `r bw("MUN", "k-fold")` and `r bw("MUN", "forward")`;
  Saved Feed `r bw("SF", "k-fold")` and `r bw("SF", "forward")`; CH4 `r bw("CH4", "k-fold")` and
  `r bw("CH4", "forward")`.
  `r if ("NUE_rg0.9" %in% best$trait) sprintf("With between-country r_g 0.9: NUE %s k-fold and %s forward.", bw("NUE_rg0.9", "k-fold"), bw("NUE_rg0.9", "forward")) else ""`
  Differences below about 0.05 are within fold-to-fold noise (one run per dataset).
* GBLUP and rrBLUP agree exactly, as theory requires. BayesA/B do not improve on GBLUP under
  this polygenic architecture.
* Weighted ssGBLUP is not recommended: after the SNP-weight iteration REML fitted h^2^ of
  `r f2(wss_h2[1])` to `r f2(wss_h2[2])` (true values are far lower), and its EBVs are strongly
  over-dispersed.
* *Real-data benchmark.* For Finnish Red cows, Chegini et al. (2026, *Front Genet*
  17:1815864) report ssGBLUP forward-validation correlations of 0.33-0.53 and dispersion
  0.45-0.75 for feed-efficiency traits. Their correlations are computed against real
  (corrected) phenotypes, so they are not the same quantity as accuracy against true breeding
  values here and cannot be ranked against it. Their dispersion range does show that
  over-dispersion of this size also occurs in real single-step evaluations.

# Multi-trait Bayesian models and GxE (file 03)

```{r mt}
mth <- rd("mt_h2.csv"); mta <- rd("mt_accuracy.csv"); mtr <- rd("mt_rg.csv")
if (!is.null(mth)) kable(dcast(mth, trait ~ model, value.var = "h2"), digits = 3, caption = "Posterior-mean h2")
if (!is.null(mtr)) kable(mtr[, .(rmse = sqrt(mean((estimated - realised)^2)),
                                 cor = cor(estimated, realised)), by = model], digits = 3,
                         caption = "Recovery of the realised genetic correlations")
if (!is.null(mta)) kable(dcast(mta[trait %in% c("NUE", "MUN", "MY", "SF")], scenario + trait ~ model,
                               value.var = "acc_TBV"), digits = 3,
                         caption = "Accuracy in the youngest generation; N_masked = NUE and MUN unrecorded")
```

```{r mt_text, include=FALSE}
nue_nm <- if (!is.null(mta)) mta[scenario == "N_masked" & trait == "NUE"][order(-acc_TBV)] else NULL
acc_s <- function(x) paste(sprintf("%s %.2f", sub("MT-", "", x$model), x$acc_TBV), collapse = ", ")
dic_best <- if (!is.null(mta) && "DIC" %in% names(mta)) unique(mta[scenario == "N_masked", .(model, DIC)])[which.min(DIC), sub("MT-", "", model)] else NA
```

**Multi-trait reading.** Two separate questions:

* *Prediction:* when NUE and MUN are unrecorded on young cows but their other traits are
  recorded (`N_masked`), NUE accuracy was `r acc_s(nue_nm)`; the most accurate model was
  `r sub("MT-", "", nue_nm$model[1])`, and DIC was lowest for `r dic_best`. Only models whose
  accuracy exceeds DIAG (no genetic covariances) gain from the correlations.
* *Parameter estimation:* with 1,500 cows and `r if (!is.null(mth)) uniqueN(mth$trait) else 11` traits, posterior heritabilities are pulled
  towards the prior (compressed range: `r if (!is.null(mth)) sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", min(mth$h2), max(mth$h2)) else "n/a"`
  against true values of `r if (!is.null(vc)) sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", min(vc$h2_true_genotyped), max(vc$h2_true_genotyped)) else "n/a"`)
  and genetic correlations are shrunk towards zero (slope of estimated on realised r~g~:
  `r if (!is.null(mtr)) paste(mtr[, .(b = coef(lm(estimated ~ realised))[2]), by = model][, sprintf("%s %.2f", sub("MT-", "", model), b)], collapse = ", ") else "n/a"`), though
  their pattern is recovered`r if (!is.null(mtr)) paste0(" (correlation between estimated and realised r_g: ", paste(mtr[, .(c = cor(estimated, realised)), by = model][, sprintf("%s %.2f", sub("MT-", "", model), c)], collapse = ", "), ")") else ""`. These Bayesian (co)variances should not be used as parameter
  estimates at this data size; the single-trait REML values in Section 3 are more reliable.

```{r gxe}
g1 <- rd("gxe_models.csv"); g9 <- rd("gxe_models.csv", params$gxe_dir)
gx <- rbindlist(list(if (!is.null(g1)) cbind(data = "no GxE simulated (r_g = 1, control)", g1),
                     if (!is.null(g9)) cbind(data = "GxE simulated (r_g = 0.9)", g9)), fill = TRUE)
if (nrow(gx)) kable(gx[, .(data, trait, model, LRT, df, p_LRT, rg_between, rg_se, rg_upper95, true_rg)],
                    digits = 3, caption = "GxE: likelihood-ratio tests against the no-GxE model")
b1 <- rd("gxe_bayes.csv"); b9 <- rd("gxe_bayes.csv", params$gxe_dir)
gb <- rbindlist(list(if (!is.null(b1)) cbind(data = "no GxE simulated (r_g = 1, control)", b1),
                     if (!is.null(b9)) cbind(data = "GxE simulated (r_g = 0.9)", b9)), fill = TRUE)
if (nrow(gb)) kable(gb[, .(data, trait, prior_mean_rg, rg_mean, rg_lower95, rg_upper95, true_rg)], digits = 3,
                    caption = "Bayesian multi-country model: posterior mean between-country r_g under two opposite priors")
v1 <- rd("gxe_bayes_verdict.csv"); v9 <- rd("gxe_bayes_verdict.csv", params$gxe_dir)
gv <- rbindlist(list(if (!is.null(v1)) cbind(data = "control (r_g = 1)", v1),
                     if (!is.null(v9)) cbind(data = "GxE (r_g = 0.9)", v9)), fill = TRUE)
if (nrow(gv)) kable(gv, caption = "GxE verdict (both priors must agree)")
```

```{r gxe_text, include=FALSE}
lrt <- if (nrow(gx)) gx[model != "M1_main"] else data.table()
lrt_s <- function(d) { x <- lrt[grepl(d, data)]
  paste(sprintf("%s p %s (%s)", x$trait, ifelse(x$p_LRT < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("= %.3f", x$p_LRT)),
                ifelse(x$converged, "converged", "not converged")), collapse = "; ") }
false_pos <- nrow(lrt) && lrt[grepl("control", data) & p_LRT < 0.05, .N] > 0
verd <- function(d) { x <- gv[grepl(d, data)]; paste(sprintf("%s: %s", x$trait, x$verdict), collapse = "; ") }
```

**GxE reading.** REML likelihood-ratio tests of the compound-symmetry model against no GxE:
on the control data (no GxE simulated) `r lrt_s("control")`; on the data simulated with
r~g~ = 0.9 `r lrt_s("0.9")`. `r rule_ctrl <- lrt[grepl("control", data) & p_LRT < 0.05 & rg_upper95 < 0.8, .N]; if (false_pos) sprintf("The likelihood-ratio test alone flagged GxE on the control data, where none was simulated (a false positive); the full rule of file 03, which also requires the upper 95%% limit of r_g below 0.80, %s.", if (rule_ctrl == 0) "did not declare it" else "declared it as well") else "No false GxE was flagged on the control data."`
`r if (nrow(lrt) && any(!lrt$converged)) sprintf("%d of %d of these fits did not converge within the iteration cap (file 03, gxe_reml_iter), so their likelihood-ratio tests are not reliable.", lrt[converged == FALSE, .N], nrow(lrt)) else ""`
Standard errors of the between-country r~g~ were `r if (nrow(lrt)) sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", min(lrt$rg_se, na.rm = TRUE), max(lrt$rg_se, na.rm = TRUE)) else "n/a"`.
The Bayesian verdict (both priors must agree) was - control: `r verd("control")`; GxE data: `r verd("0.9")`.
Estimating GxE of this size needs far more genotyped and recorded cows per country than the
1,500-cow subsample used here. The GxE dataset came from a separate coalescent run, so its
accuracies are not a paired comparison with the control dataset.

# Breeding programmes over time (file 04)

```{r load04}
trend <- rbindlist(lapply(scen, function(s) rd(sprintf("gs_trend_%s.csv", s))), fill = TRUE)
beq   <- rbindlist(lapply(scen, function(s) rd(sprintf("gs_breeders_equation_%s.csv", s))), fill = TRUE)
idx   <- rbindlist(lapply(scen, function(s) rd(sprintf("gs_index_correlations_%s.csv", s))), fill = TRUE)
Fdt   <- rbindlist(lapply(scen, function(s) rd(sprintf("gs_inbreeding_%s.csv", s))), fill = TRUE)
t0    <- rd("trend_burnin.csv")
tr_all <- rbind(rbindlist(lapply(scen, function(s) cbind(scenario = s, t0))), trend, fill = TRUE)
tr_all[, scenario := factor(scenario, scen)]
```

## Mean and variance of genetic and phenotypic values

```{r trends, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
key <- c("NUE", "MUN", "CH4", "MY", "PY", "SF")
long <- melt(tr_all[trait %in% key & breed == "HOL"],
             id.vars = c("scenario", "generation", "breed", "trait"))
ggplot(long, aes(generation, value, colour = scenario)) + geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = max(t0$generation) + 0.5, lty = 3) + scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  facet_grid(variable ~ trait, scales = "free_y") + theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Holstein: mean and variance of genetic (G) and phenotypic (P) values",
       subtitle = "generations 0-10 = phenotypic burn-in; dotted line = start of the programmes (replicate 0)",
       y = "founder genetic SD units")
```

```{r final_table}
fin <- tr_all[generation == max(generation) & trait %in% c(key, "SCS", "LNVAR", "ICF", "LONG")]
kable(dcast(fin, breed + trait ~ scenario, value.var = "mean_G"), digits = 2,
      caption = "Mean genetic value in the final generation")
gain <- merge(tr_all[generation == max(t0$generation), .(breed, trait, scenario, start = mean_G)],
              tr_all[generation == max(generation), .(breed, trait, scenario, end = mean_G)])
gain[, response := end - start]
kable(dcast(gain[trait %in% key], breed + trait ~ scenario,
            value.var = "response"), digits = 2,
      caption = "Response over the 10 selection generations (end minus last burn-in generation), replicate 0")
```

## Breeder's equation: expected vs observed response

```{r beq}
beq[, dG_observed := shift(meanH, type = "lead") - meanH, by = .(scenario, breed)]
kable(beq[, .(i_sires_theory = mean(i_male_theory), i_sires = mean(i_male_obs),
              i_dams_of_sons = mean(i_elite_obs), i_dams_of_daughters = mean(i_female_obs),
              r_m = mean(r_male), r_f = mean(r_female), S_male = mean(S_male),
              dG_expected = mean(dG_expected), dG_observed = mean(dG_observed, na.rm = TRUE)),
          by = .(scenario, breed)], digits = 3,
      caption = "Selection intensity (i), selection differential (S), accuracy (r), expected and observed response per generation (each scenario's own index)")
ggplot(beq[!is.na(dG_observed)], aes(dG_expected, dG_observed, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_abline(lty = 2) + geom_point() + scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  facet_wrap(~breed) + theme_bw() + labs(title = "Four-path breeder's equation vs simulation")
```

The response is measured on each scenario's **own** index, so ΔG values are not comparable
*between* scenarios; the trait-level table above is the like-for-like comparison.

  pk(dcast(idx[, .(acc = mean(acc_trait)), by = .(scenario, trait)], trait ~ scenario,

}

## Inbreeding

```{r inb, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
ggplot(Fdt, aes(generation, F_genomic, colour = scenario)) + geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.06, lty = 2) + scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  facet_wrap(~breed) + theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "mean genomic F relative to end of burn-in", subtitle = "dashed = 6% target from the pipeline figure")
kable(dcast(Fdt[generation == max(generation)], breed ~ scenario, value.var = "F_genomic"), digits = 3,
      caption = "Genomic inbreeding after 10 generations of selection (level relative to the multi-breed base)")
# rate of inbreeding per generation: 1 - ((1 - F_T) / (1 - F_0))^(1/T), from the first to the last generation
dF <- Fdt[, .(F0 = F_genomic[generation == min(generation)], FT = F_genomic[generation == max(generation)],
              T = max(generation) - min(generation)), by = .(scenario, breed)]
dF[, dF_per_gen := 1 - ((1 - FT) / (1 - F0))^(1 / T)]
kable(dcast(dF, breed ~ scenario, value.var = "dF_per_gen"), digits = 4,
      caption = "Rate of inbreeding per generation, replicate 0 (FAO guideline: at most 0.01; OCS target: 0.01)")
ocs <- rbindlist(lapply(0:(params$n_rep - 1), function(r) rd(sprintf("gs_ocs_GS_NTM_NUE35_OCS_dF1%s.csv", if (r == 0) "" else paste0("_rep", r)), rep_dir(r))), fill = TRUE)
if (nrow(ocs)) kable(ocs[, .(feasible = all(feasible), mean_sires_used = mean(n_sires_used),
                                 max_sire_share = max(max_share),
                                 max_gap_to_target = max(C_achieved - C_target)), by = .(scenario, breed)],
                         digits = 4, caption = "OCS: every generation on target? sires used, largest sire share")
```

# Replicates: how robust are the scenario differences?

The six main scenarios were each run on up to `r params$n_rep` replicates. **Each replicate has its own
coalescent founder population and burn-in** (file 01 with `rep_id` r: seed + r, which also changes the
MaCS seed), so the spread between replicates now includes founder sampling, Mendelian sampling,
phenotypes, training samples and matings. The same founders and seed are used for every scenario
within a replicate, so differences are **paired**.

**NTM value of a response.** For each breed, the genetic change in each trait is divided by its
standardisation SD (file 04, `gs_sdA0.csv`), multiplied by that breed's GS_NTM weight and by 10
(NTM index units per SD), and summed: the change in the *simulated part* of NTM. Multiplied by
EUR per NTM unit (HOL 9.9, RDC 9.2, JER 8.0 per cow-year; Fikse & Kargo 2020) it is the extra
income per cow-year of daughters at the end, excluding non-simulated sub-indices.

```{r replicates, results="asis"}
rep_sc <- c("GS_NTM", "GS_NTM_NUE35", "GS_NTM_NUE75", "GS_NTM_NUE35_MUN", ch4_sc, "GS_NTM_NUE35_OCS_dF1")
R <- 0:(params$n_rep - 1)
read_rep <- function(kind, s, r, dir = rep_dir(r))
  rd(sprintf("gs_%s_%s%s.csv", kind, s, if (r == 0) "" else paste0("_rep", r)), dir)
w_ntm <- iw[index == "GS_NTM"]
# response = final generation minus the last burn-in generation OF THE SAME REPLICATE
resp_of <- function(s, r, dir = rep_dir(r)) {
  tr <- read_rep("trend", s, r, dir); tb <- rd("trend_burnin.csv", dir); if (is.null(tr) || is.null(tb)) return(NULL)
  merge(tr[generation == max(generation), .(breed, trait, end = mean_G)],
        tb[generation == max(generation), .(breed, trait, start = mean_G)], by = c("breed", "trait"))[, response := end - start][]
}
reps <- rbindlist(lapply(rep_sc, function(s) rbindlist(lapply(R, function(r) {
  resp <- resp_of(s, r); Fd <- read_rep("inbreeding", s, r); sdA0 <- rd("gs_sdA0.csv", rep_dir(r))
  if (is.null(resp) || is.null(Fd) || is.null(sdA0)) return(NULL)
  v <- merge(merge(resp, sdA0, by = "trait"), w_ntm[, .(breed, trait, w = weight)], by = c("breed", "trait"))
  ntm <- v[, .(NTM = 10 * sum(w * response / sdA0)), by = breed][, EUR := NTM * eur_per_ntm[breed]]
  dF <- Fd[, .(dF = 1 - ((1 - F_genomic[generation == max(generation)]) /
                           (1 - F_genomic[generation == min(generation)]))^(1 / (max(generation) - min(generation)))),
           by = breed]
  out <- dcast(resp[trait %in% c("NUE", "MUN", "CH4", "MY", "PY", "SF", "SCS", "ICF", "LONG")], breed ~ trait, value.var = "response")
  Reduce(function(a, b) merge(a, b, by = "breed"), list(out, ntm, dF))[, `:=`(scenario = s, replicate = r)]
}))))
if (nrow(reps)) {
  # tidy copies for the spreadsheet (NUE_replicate_results.xlsx)
  rep_long <- rbindlist(lapply(rep_sc, function(s) rbindlist(lapply(R, function(r) {
    x <- resp_of(s, r); if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    x[trait %in% c("NUE", "MUN", "CH4", "MY", "PY", "SF")][, `:=`(scenario = s, replicate = r,
      source = sprintf("%s/gs_trend_%s%s.csv", rep_dir(r), s, if (r == 0) "" else paste0("_rep", r)))]
  }))))
  fwrite(rep_long, file.path(params$base_dir, "replicate_response_long.csv"))
  fwrite(reps[, .(scenario, replicate, breed, dF, NTM, EUR,
                  source = sprintf("%s/gs_inbreeding_%s%s.csv", sapply(replicate, rep_dir), scenario, ifelse(replicate == 0, "", paste0("_rep", replicate))))],
         file.path(params$base_dir, "replicate_dF.csv"))
  pk(reps[, .(n = uniqueN(replicate)), by = scenario], caption = "Replicates available per scenario")
  long <- melt(reps, id.vars = c("scenario", "replicate", "breed"))
  pk(dcast(long[, .(txt = if (.BY$variable == "dF") sprintf("%.4f +/- %.4f", mean(value), sd(value)) else sprintf("%.2f +/- %.2f", mean(value), sd(value))), by = .(scenario, breed, variable)],
              breed + variable ~ scenario, value.var = "txt"),
        caption = "Response over 10 selection generations (genetic SD; NTM = index units; EUR = per cow-year) and rate of inbreeding (dF): mean +/- SD over replicates")
  pair_test <- function(a, b, v) {
    w <- merge(reps[scenario == a, c("replicate", "breed", v), with = FALSE],
               reps[scenario == b, c("replicate", "breed", v), with = FALSE], by = c("replicate", "breed"))
    if (nrow(w) == 0) return(NULL)
    w[, d := get(paste0(v, ".x")) - get(paste0(v, ".y"))]
    w[, .(n = .N, mean_diff = mean(d), sd_diff = sd(d), same_sign = max(sum(d > 0), sum(d < 0)),
          p_paired = if (.N > 1 && sd(d) > 0) t.test(d)$p.value else NA_real_), by = breed][, comparison := paste(a, "-", b)][, trait := v][]
  }
  pt <- rbindlist(lapply(c("NUE", "MUN", "CH4", "MY", "PY", "SF", "NTM", "EUR", "dF"), function(v) rbind(
    pair_test("GS_NTM_NUE35", "GS_NTM", v), pair_test("GS_NTM_NUE75", "GS_NTM", v),
    pair_test("GS_NTM_NUE35_MUN", "GS_NTM_NUE35", v), pair_test(ch4_sc, ch4_base, v),
    pair_test("GS_NTM_NUE35_OCS_dF1", "GS_NTM_NUE35", v))))
  pk(pt[, .(comparison, trait, breed, n, mean_diff, sd_diff, same_sign, p_paired)], digits = 4,
        caption = "Table A (p-values only). Paired differences between scenarios (same seed within replicate); same_sign = replicates with the majority sign; paired t-test, uncorrected")
  # 13 Nov 2026 (my decision): correction for multiple testing. One family = all paired tests of this section.
  # EUR is NTM times a constant per breed (the same test), so it is not counted twice and takes the NTM values.
  fam <- pt[trait != "EUR" & !is.na(p_paired)]
  fam[, `:=`(p_BH = p.adjust(p_paired, method = "BH"), p_Bonferroni = p.adjust(p_paired, method = "bonferroni"))]
  pt[fam, on = .(comparison, trait, breed), `:=`(p_BH = i.p_BH, p_Bonferroni = i.p_Bonferroni)]
  pt[fam[trait == "NTM"][, trait := "EUR"], on = .(comparison, trait, breed), `:=`(p_BH = i.p_BH, p_Bonferroni = i.p_Bonferroni)]
  n_fam <- nrow(fam)
  fwrite(pt, file.path(params$base_dir, "paired_tests_multiple_testing.csv"))
  pk(pt[, .(comparison, trait, breed, n, mean_diff, p_paired, p_BH, p_Bonferroni)], digits = 4,
     caption = sprintf("Table B (p-values + corrections). The same tests with Benjamini-Hochberg (false discovery rate) and Bonferroni adjusted p-values; family of %d tests (EUR rows repeat NTM)", n_fam))
  mt_count <- rbind(fam[, .(comparison = "All comparisons", tests = .N, uncorrected = sum(p_paired < 0.05), BH = sum(p_BH < 0.05), Bonferroni = sum(p_Bonferroni < 0.05))],
                    fam[, .(tests = .N, uncorrected = sum(p_paired < 0.05), BH = sum(p_BH < 0.05), Bonferroni = sum(p_Bonferroni < 0.05)), by = comparison])
  pk(mt_count, caption = "Table C. Number of tests significant at 5% under each method")
  verdict <- function(x) ifelse(x < 0.05, "yes", "no")
  key <- fam[(comparison == "GS_NTM_NUE35 - GS_NTM" & trait %in% c("NUE", "NTM")) | (comparison == "GS_NTM_NUE75 - GS_NTM" & trait %in% c("NUE", "NTM")) |
             (comparison == "GS_NTM_NUE35_MUN - GS_NTM_NUE35" & trait %in% c("MUN", "NUE", "NTM")) |
             (comparison == paste(ch4_sc, "-", ch4_base) & trait %in% c("CH4", "NTM")) |
             (comparison == "GS_NTM_NUE35_OCS_dF1 - GS_NTM_NUE35" & trait %in% c("dF", "NTM", "NUE"))]
  pk(key[, .(comparison, trait, breed, mean_diff, p_paired, uncorrected = verdict(p_paired), BH = verdict(p_BH), Bonferroni = verdict(p_Bonferroni))], digits = 4,
     caption = "Table D. Headline results: significant at 5% under each method?")
  lost <- fam[p_paired < 0.05 & p_BH >= 0.05][order(p_paired)]
  pk(lost[, .(comparison, trait, breed, mean_diff, p_paired, p_BH)], digits = 4,
     caption = "Table E. Results below 0.05 uncorrected that do not pass Benjamini-Hochberg (to be read as not established)")
}
```

**Multiple testing (13 Nov 2026).** The section runs `r if (exists("n_fam")) n_fam else NA` paired tests, so about
`r if (exists("n_fam")) round(0.05 * n_fam) else NA` would fall below 0.05 by chance if no scenario differed. Three readings are given:

| Method | Controls | Rule | Strength | Weakness here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Uncorrected p (Table A) | Error rate of each single test | p < 0.05 | Most power | Many tests: some "significant" results are chance |
| Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) | False discovery rate: expected share of false results among those declared significant | adjusted p < 0.05 | Keeps power with many tests; proven for independent or positively dependent tests (Benjamini & Hochberg 1995; Benjamini & Yekutieli 2001) | Allows about 5% of the declared results to be false |
| Bonferroni | Family-wise error rate: probability of even one false result | p x number of tests < 0.05 | Strictest guarantee | Assumes the worst case; very low power with 10 replicates and correlated tests |

**Preferred for this study: Benjamini-Hochberg.** The tests are many and dependent (the same 10 replicates, genetically correlated traits),
the aim is to screen which scenario differences are consistent rather than to confirm one hypothesis, and replicates are few,
so Bonferroni would hide real differences. BH is proven to control the false discovery rate for independent or positively
dependent tests; under other forms of dependence it is not guaranteed, which is a further reason to show Bonferroni next to it. Bonferroni is shown as the
conservative bound: a result that passes it is beyond reasonable doubt in this simulation. The p-values quoted in the
breeding-plan section below are uncorrected; a difference listed in Table E should be read as **not established**.

With n replicates the paired t-test has n - 1 degrees of freedom. All three readings describe consistency across
simulated founder populations, not a formal claim about real populations.

**Simulation vs selection-index theory.** The ratio of NUE responses (NUE index / NTM index)
from the simulation is compared with the ratio expected from file 00 (true breeding values,
infinite population). Agreement checks that the simulated programme behaves as the index
design intends; differences come from EBV accuracy, finite population and changing variances.

```{r theory_check}
if (nrow(reps)) {
  sim_ratio <- reps[, .(NUE = mean(NUE), NTM = mean(NTM)), by = .(scenario, breed)]
  sim_ratio <- merge(sim_ratio[scenario %in% c("GS_NTM_NUE35", "GS_NTM_NUE75")],
                     sim_ratio[scenario == "GS_NTM", .(breed, NUE0 = NUE, NTM0 = NTM)], by = "breed")
  sim_ratio[, nue_weight := ifelse(scenario == "GS_NTM_NUE35", 0.35, 0.75)]
  th <- merge(fr[nue_weight %in% c(0.35, 0.75), .(breed, nue_weight, NUE_th = NUE, NTM_th = NTM_pct_of_max / 100)],
              fr[nue_weight == 0, .(breed, NUE0_th = NUE)], by = "breed")
  cmp_th <- merge(sim_ratio, th, by = c("breed", "nue_weight"))
  kable(cmp_th[, .(breed, scenario, NUE_ratio_sim = NUE / NUE0, NUE_ratio_theory = NUE_th / NUE0_th,
                   NTM_ratio_sim = NTM / NTM0, NTM_ratio_theory = NTM_th)], digits = 3,
        caption = "NUE and NTM response relative to GS_NTM: simulation (replicate means) vs selection-index theory")
}
```

# Sensitivity: how much do the conclusions rest on the NUE correlations?

Every NUE correlation was multiplied by s = 0 and s = 0.5 (file 00; s = 1 is the main run), and new
founders, burn-ins and the GS_NTM and GS_NTM_NUE35 programmes were run for each level (up to
`r params$n_sens_rep` replicates per level). s = 0 means NUE is genetically unrelated to every other trait.
A third set uses the heritability of the NAV Saved Feed index itself, 0.08 (Lidauer et al., NAV workshop
2026), instead of 0.23 (ReFI) (my choice, 7 Nov 2026).

```{r sensitivity, results="asis"}
sens_dir <- function(set, r) paste0(params$base_dir, if (set == "main") "" else paste0("_", set), if (r == 0) "" else paste0("_rep", r))
sens <- rbindlist(lapply(c("NUEx0", "NUEx05", "SFh008", "main"), function(set) rbindlist(lapply(0:(params$n_sens_rep - 1), function(r)
  rbindlist(lapply(c("GS_NTM", "GS_NTM_NUE35"), function(s) {
    x <- resp_of(s, r, sens_dir(set, r)); sd0 <- rd("gs_sdA0.csv", sens_dir(set, r))
    if (is.null(x) || is.null(sd0)) return(NULL)
    v <- merge(merge(x, sd0, by = "trait"), w_ntm[, .(breed, trait, w = weight)], by = c("breed", "trait"))
    merge(merge(x[trait == "NUE", .(breed, NUE = response)], x[trait == "SF", .(breed, SF = response)], by = "breed"),
          v[, .(NTM = 10 * sum(w * response / sdA0)), by = breed], by = "breed")[
      , `:=`(set = set, replicate = r, scenario = s)]
  }))))), fill = TRUE)
if (nrow(sens)) {
  sens[, set_label := c(NUEx0 = "NUE correlations x 0", NUEx05 = "NUE correlations x 0.5",
                        SFh008 = "Saved Feed h2 0.08", main = "main run")[set]]
  sw2 <- dcast(sens, set_label + breed + replicate ~ scenario, value.var = c("NUE", "SF", "NTM"))
  sw2[, `:=`(dNUE = NUE_GS_NTM_NUE35 - NUE_GS_NTM, dNTM = NTM_GS_NTM_NUE35 - NTM_GS_NTM)]
  sens_tab <- sw2[, .(n = .N, NUE_under_NTM = mean(NUE_GS_NTM), SF_under_NTM = mean(SF_GS_NTM),
                      NUE_gain_from_weight = mean(dNUE),
                      p_NUE = if (.N > 1 && sd(dNUE) > 0) t.test(dNUE)$p.value else NA_real_,
                      NTM_change = mean(dNTM)), by = .(set_label, breed)][order(breed, set_label)]
  pk(sens_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Sensitivity sets: NUE and Saved Feed response under NTM alone, extra NUE from the 0.35 weight, and NTM change (paired within replicate)")
  th_s <- fread("params/nue_sensitivity_theory.csv")
  pk(th_s, digits = 3, caption = "The same comparison from selection-index theory (file 00)")
}
```

**Reading.** If the NUE gain *under NTM alone* falls towards 0 as s goes to 0, NTM improves NUE only
through the correlations, and the claim "NTM already improves NUE" depends on the Irish estimates. If the
extra gain from the NUE weight stays clearly positive at every s, the recommendation to add an NUE weight
does not depend on them.

# Recommended breeding plan

Every number in this section is computed from the replicate table above (`r uniqueN(reps$replicate)` paired replicates,
mean difference and paired t-test p per breed), or read from files 00-03. The parameters it
rests on are listed in file 00 and the README.

```{r plan_helpers, include=FALSE}
fd <- function(cmp, v, d = 2) {                 # "HOL +0.52 (p = 0.06), JER ..." from pt
  x <- pt[comparison == cmp & trait == v][order(breed)]
  paste(sprintf("%s %+.*f (p %s)", x$breed, d, x$mean_diff,
                ifelse(x$p_paired < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("= %.3f", x$p_paired))), collapse = ", ")
}
rng <- function(cmp, v, d = 2) { x <- pt[comparison == cmp & trait == v]$mean_diff
  sprintf("%.*f to %.*f", d, min(x), d, max(x)) }
mdF <- function(s) { x <- reps[scenario == s, .(m = mean(dF)), by = breed]$m
  sprintf("%.1f%% to %.1f%%", 100 * min(x), 100 * max(x)) }
mv <- function(s, v, d = 2) { x <- reps[scenario == s, .(m = mean(get(v))), by = breed][order(breed)]
  paste(sprintf("%s %.*f", x$breed, d, x$m), collapse = ", ") }
# item 2: data-driven verdict on the NUE weight (added 3 Nov 2026, after the 5-replicate runs)
n_sig <- function(cmp, v, dir = 1) pt[comparison == cmp & trait == v & p_paired < 0.05 & sign(mean_diff) == dir, .N]
nue35_sig <- n_sig("GS_NTM_NUE35 - GS_NTM", "NUE"); nue75_sig <- n_sig("GS_NTM_NUE75 - GS_NTM", "NUE")
ntm_sig <- pt[grepl("^GS_NTM_NUE(35|75) - GS_NTM$", comparison) & trait == "NTM" & p_paired < 0.05, .N]
# expected NTM loss after 10 generations = (1 - theory share kept) x simulated GS_NTM response;
# replicates needed to detect it (paired, two-sided 5%, power 80%): ((1.96 + 0.84) sd_diff / loss)^2
ntm0 <- reps[scenario == "GS_NTM", .(NTM0 = mean(NTM)), by = breed]
det <- merge(merge(fr[nue_weight %in% c(0.35, 0.75), .(breed, nue_weight, kept = NTM_pct_of_max / 100)], ntm0, by = "breed"),
             pt[trait == "NTM" & grepl("^GS_NTM_NUE(35|75) - GS_NTM$", comparison),
                .(breed, nue_weight = ifelse(grepl("35", comparison), 0.35, 0.75), sd_diff, mean_diff)],
             by = c("breed", "nue_weight"))[, `:=`(loss = (1 - kept) * NTM0, se = sd_diff / sqrt(uniqueN(reps$replicate)))][
             , n_need := ceiling(((1.96 + 0.84) * sd_diff / loss)^2)]
det_txt <- function(w, col, d = 1) { x <- det[nue_weight == w][order(breed)]
  paste(sprintf("%s %.*f", x$breed, d, x[[col]]), collapse = ", ") }
acc_ix <- rbindlist(lapply(R, function(r) read_rep("index_correlations", "GS_NTM", r)), fill = TRUE)
acc_txt <- function(v) { x <- acc_ix[trait == v, .(a = mean(acc_trait)), by = breed]$a
  sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", min(x), max(x)) }
th_gap <- if (exists("cmp_th")) cmp_th[, .(breed, nue_weight, gap = NUE_th / NUE0_th - NUE / NUE0)] else NULL
th_txt <- function(w) { x <- cmp_th[nue_weight == w][order(breed)]
  paste(sprintf("%s %.2f vs %.2f", x$breed, x$NUE / x$NUE0, x$NUE_th / x$NUE0_th), collapse = ", ") }
```

1. **Evaluation model.** `r mt <- if (file.exists("params/eval_model_test.csv")) fread("params/eval_model_test.csv") else NULL; ss_near <- cvs[!is.na(acc_wb) & model %in% c("ssGBLUP", "ssGBLUP_MF"), .(ok = max(acc_wb) >= cvs[trait == .BY$trait & scheme == .BY$scheme, max(acc_wb, na.rm = TRUE)] - 0.05), by = .(trait, scheme)]; ""`
   *Cross-validation (file 02):* a single-step model (pooled-adjusted or metafounder) was the best
   model or within 0.05 of the best in `r sum(ss_near$ok)` of `r nrow(ss_near)` trait x validation-scheme
   comparisons. *Inside the breeding programme (04b, 2 replicates of GS_NTM_NUE35):*
   `r if (!is.null(mt)) paste(ifelse(is.finite(mt$eval_sec_per_gen), sprintf("%s: NTM %+.2f, NUE %+.2f, %.0f s per evaluation (x%.1f)", mt$model, mt$NTM, mt$NUE, mt$eval_sec_per_gen, mt$time_ratio_vs_SNPBLUP), sprintf("%s: could not be run (killed for exceeding the ~6.1 GB memory limit of the local machine, 8 Nov 2026)", mt$model)), collapse = "; ") else "not available"`,
   so **`r eval_model`** was used for all replicate runs (rule: ssGBLUP only if higher NTM and
   not lower NUE response at no more than twice the run time). For routine evaluation the single-step
   family remains the standard because it uses cows that have CFIT records but no genotypes; within
   it, the compatibility method chosen in file 02 is listed in the cross-validation section.
   Weighted ssGBLUP should not be used (over-dispersed EBVs).
2. **Selection index: NTM already improves NUE. An added NUE weight raised NUE further
   (significant in `r nue75_sig` of 3 breeds at 0.75, `r nue35_sig` of 3 at 0.35); its cost in
   NTM was `r if (ntm_sig == 0) paste("not detectable in", uniqueN(reps$replicate), "replicates and is known only from theory") else paste("significant in", ntm_sig, "breed x weight comparisons")`.**
   Over 10 generations, in genetic SD (NTM and EUR: genetic level after 10 generations,
   EUR per cow-year):
   * Under NTM alone (GS_NTM), NUE rose by `r mv("GS_NTM", "NUE")`, carried by protein yield
     (r~g~ PY-NUE 0.80, Tavernier et al. 2024).
   * Adding NUE at 0.35 (GS_NTM_NUE35 - GS_NTM): NUE `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE35 - GS_NTM", "NUE")`;
     NTM value `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE35 - GS_NTM", "NTM", 1)` index units, i.e.
     `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE35 - GS_NTM", "EUR", 1)` EUR per cow-year.
   * Adding NUE at 0.75 (GS_NTM_NUE75 - GS_NTM): NUE `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE75 - GS_NTM", "NUE")`;
     NTM value `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE75 - GS_NTM", "NTM", 1)` index units, i.e.
     `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE75 - GS_NTM", "EUR", 1)` EUR per cow-year.
   * Correlated changes at weight 0.35: CH4 `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE35 - GS_NTM", "CH4")`;
     MUN `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE35 - GS_NTM", "MUN")`; milk yield `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE35 - GS_NTM", "MY")`.
     Because the two indices differ only in the NUE weight, these are effects of that weight.
   * Correlated changes at weight 0.75: CH4 `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE75 - GS_NTM", "CH4")`;
     protein yield `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE75 - GS_NTM", "PY")`; Saved Feed `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE75 - GS_NTM", "SF")`.
   * Under NTM alone, methane concentration *rose* (`r mv("GS_NTM", "CH4")`), through its
     sourced positive correlations with yield (Schneider et al. 2025). NTM has no methane weight.
   * **Why the NTM cost is not seen.** Selection-index theory (file 00) puts the NTM loss after
     10 generations at about `r det_txt(0.35, "loss")` index units at weight 0.35 and
     `r det_txt(0.75, "loss")` at 0.75. The replicate-to-replicate SD of the paired NTM
     difference was `r det_txt(0.35, "sd_diff")` (0.35) and `r det_txt(0.75, "sd_diff")` (0.75),
     so `r uniqueN(reps$replicate)` replicates `r if (ntm_sig == 0) "could not" else "could partly"` separate the loss from zero. To detect it (paired test, 5%,
     power 80%) would take about `r det_txt(0.75, "n_need", 0)` replicates at weight 0.75 and
     `r det_txt(0.35, "n_need", 0)` at 0.35. The positive NTM differences in some breeds cannot
     be distinguished from noise and are not evidence of a gain.
   * **Simulation vs theory for NUE.** NUE response relative to GS_NTM (simulated vs theory)
     was `r th_txt(0.35)` at 0.35 and `r th_txt(0.75)` at 0.75.
     `r gap <- cmp_th[, NUE / NUE0 - NUE_th / NUE0_th]; if (max(abs(gap)) <= 0.05) sprintf("The simulated and theoretical ratios agree within %.2f in every breed, so the simulated programme behaves as the index design intends.", max(abs(gap))) else sprintf("The largest gap is %.2f. Where the simulated gain is smaller than theory, this is consistent with selection on EBVs: theory assumes true breeding values, while under GS_NTM the accuracy of the cows' EBVs was %s for NUE against %s for protein yield, so part of the NUE weight is lost to prediction error (not tested directly).", max(abs(gap)), acc_txt("NUE"), acc_txt("PY"))`
   Which weight to use is a price decision for the breeding organisation. Because the simulated
   NTM cost is within noise, the price to use is the theoretical one in file 00 (EUR per cow-year
   per unit selection intensity). The EUR figures cover only the simulated part of NTM (see
   "What would change these conclusions").
3. **MUN weight (GS_NTM_NUE35_MUN - GS_NTM_NUE35).** Adding MUN at -0.35 on top of NUE 0.35 changed
   NUE by `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE35_MUN - GS_NTM_NUE35", "NUE")` and MUN by
   `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE35_MUN - GS_NTM_NUE35", "MUN")`, at an NTM cost of
   `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE35_MUN - GS_NTM_NUE35", "EUR", 1)` EUR per cow-year. Correa-Luna et al. (2021)
   found that low-MUN breeding values did not improve NUE, and the relation of MUN to urinary N is
   phenotypic, diet-driven and breed-specific (Mangwe et al. 2025; Burren et al. 2025), so a MUN weight
   is justified only if urinary N or ammonia gets its own value in the breeding goal.
4. **Methane weight (`r ch4_sc` - `r ch4_base`).** The CH4 weight `r idx_def[index == ch4_sc, ch4]` is the knee of the
   sweep in file 00 (largest CH4 reduction per % NTM given up, selection-index theory). In the
   simulation it changed CH4 by `r fd(paste(ch4_sc, "-", ch4_base), "CH4")`, NUE by
   `r fd(paste(ch4_sc, "-", ch4_base), "NUE")` and NTM value by
   `r fd(paste(ch4_sc, "-", ch4_base), "EUR", 1)` EUR per cow-year. Under NTM alone CH4 rose
   (`r mv("GS_NTM", "CH4")`). Real-world context: Nordic and Norwegian evaluations of methane are being
   developed from sniffer and GreenFeed data (Heringstad et al., ICAR 2026; Nielsen et al., ICAR 2026);
   the CH4 trait here is a concentration-type trait with the correlations of file 00, so the size of
   the response depends on those parameters.
5. **One joint evaluation across Denmark, Sweden, Finland and Germany**, unless a GxE test on
   real data shows a between-country r~g~ credibly below 0.80. In this simulation GxE of
   r~g~ = 0.9 could not be estimated precisely from the subsample`r if (false_pos) ", and the likelihood-ratio test alone flagged GxE on the control data where none was simulated" else ""` (see the GxE section).
6. **Optimum contribution selection with ΔF = 1% per generation, then mate allocation.**
   Unconstrained genomic selection on the NTM + NUE 0.35 index raised inbreeding by
   `r mdF("GS_NTM_NUE35")` per generation; OCS at 1% brought this to
   `r mdF("GS_NTM_NUE35_OCS_dF1")`. The cost was NUE `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE35_OCS_dF1 - GS_NTM_NUE35", "NUE")`
   and NTM value `r fd("GS_NTM_NUE35_OCS_dF1 - GS_NTM_NUE35", "EUR", 1)` EUR per cow-year.
   `r ma <- dF[scenario == "GS_NTM_NUE35_MATE"]; nm <- dF[scenario == "GS_NTM_NUE35"]; if (nrow(ma)) sprintf("Mate allocation alone (single run) lowered genomic F after 10 generations (%s vs %s without it) but its rate of inbreeding was still %.1f%% to %.1f%% per generation, above the 1%% guideline (inbreeding section).", paste(sprintf("%s %.2f", ma$breed, ma$FT), collapse = ", "), paste(sprintf("%.2f", nm$FT[match(ma$breed, nm$breed)]), collapse = "/"), 100 * min(ma$dF_per_gen), 100 * max(ma$dF_per_gen)) else ""`
7. **Records needed**, given the low h^2^ of NUE: CFIT feed intake for N intake, plus milk
   protein and MUN from routine recording. Predicted NUE (MIR-based, Chen et al. 2021; or from
   diet energy, diet CP, milk yield and milk protein, Padberg et al. 2026, CCC 0.78) is the
   realistic phenotype; measured urinary N is not available at scale. In the multi-trait model,
   accuracy of NUE EBVs of cows without NUE records was `r acc_s(nue_nm)`: modelling the genetic
   covariances helped only in the unstructured (UN) model.

# What would change these conclusions

* Genetic correlations: `r nrow(fread("params/rg_sourced.csv"))` of 55 trait pairs are sourced
  (`rg_evidence.xlsx`; most are proxies or from Norwegian Red, Polish or Dutch cattle rather than
  the simulated breeds); the rest carry values implied by weighted bending, not estimates. All four
  NUE correlations come from one grazing Irish study (Tavernier et al. 2024). With a lower
  PY–NUE correlation, as Chen et al. (2021) imply for confinement Holstein, the NUE index
  would gain more NUE over the production index.
* The NTM part of the goal is partial: the simulated sub-indices carry
  `r nw <- fread("params/ntm_weights_source.csv"); sh <- sapply(c("HOL", "RDC", "JER"), function(b) 100 * sum(nw[simulated_as != "not simulated"][[b]]) / sum(nw[[b]])); paste(sprintf("%s %.0f%%", names(sh), sh), collapse = ", ")`
  of the total NTM weight (May 2026). The non-simulated
  sub-indices (calving, health, conformation, growth, youngstock survival) would take selection
  pressure, so absolute responses and EUR values here are too large; fat yield is missing from
  Yield; Jersey uses the Holstein milk:protein ratio; Saved Feed enters with its own published
  parameters (ReFI h^2^, NAV Saved Feed index correlations), not computed from ECM, body-weight change
  and DMI, because no kg-scale variances were available for that formula (file 00).
* Founder sampling: each replicate has its own founders, so this source of variation is included;
  the coalescent demography (Ne history, breed split times) is the same for all replicates.
* A full-size run (all 25,614 cows genotyped) on a cluster, which would also allow GxE to be
  estimated.
